product_from_film: Cluely is a desktop assistant that overlays a call, offers notes, definitions and follow-up questions, and stores meeting summaries with sharing and personalization.
explains_well: The demo follows one call from Listen through live notes, definitions, a follow-up draft and a stored summary.
unclear: Personalization is introduced late through dense templates, but no later answer shows how a changed preference affects assistance.
scenario: Use an assistant during a call, review its notes, draft a follow-up, share a summary and inspect personalization.
product_clear_basis: AI Desktop Assistant appears at 3s, followed by sees/hears claims and an overlaid call demo.

sound.detail: The coherent draft walks through listening controls, live notes, terms from the conversation, suggested questions, a follow-up draft, dashboard, sharing and personalization. Product names and some phrases are mistranscribed. The product’s hears-what-you-hear claim is not evidence that this reviewer heard audio; delivery, music, effects and synchronization remain unknown.
sound.visual_relation: V01–V11 are supported by matching captions and visible controls.
sound.evidence: Local 486-speech.json draft and chronological sheets; no validated listening.

categories.finding: Introduce → activate → live help → post-call draft → archive/share → personalize → brand.
Short sees/hears cards state the assistant’s proposed inputs immediately.
The category is explicit by 3s and the overlay is visible by 9s.
UI panels are enlarged, angled and highlighted while states update over the call. Exact easing and response latency unverified.
The live call anchors the first half; the white dashboard clearly marks post-call review.
Dark translucent overlays contrast with the later white archive; blue neon and cyan controls reinforce the brand.
Close-ups make definitions and controls readable; long personalization instructions remain dense.
ASR supports the spoken walkthrough and example dialogue; delivery remains unknown.
categories.reason: Text support only, no validated listening.

categories.finding: Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Presenter, call, translucent assistant, dashboard, summary and settings are visible; live execution unverified.

categories.finding: Captions and close-ups make most steps readable without sound, though simultaneity and audio recognition cannot be judged.
The overlay preserves call context, but its text sometimes sits over a participant’s face; enlarged views aid reading.
The film spends over a minute on live call help before archive and settings, giving the core interaction more time than the presets.
Conversation terms reappear as definitions and questions, then in a summary; personalization lacks an output payoff.
The demonstration may communicate convenience while the closing cheating slogans add provocation; audience response unmeasured.
Japantown and prompt engineering connect the call, generated help and follow-up material.
Recognition accuracy, latency, invisibility to others, public-link behavior and personalization effects were not independently checked. The follow-up is a draft, not a sent message.
The translucent desktop overlay and live action suggestions distinguish it from only a post-meeting summary tool.
Show the effect of one saved preference.
